question.text: Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) allow investors to participate in:

answer.text: Stock market index returns through a basket of equity shares
Government bond yields through a pooled investment structure
Real estate development projects in metropolitan cities

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Research Analyst workbook (p.34), InvITs pool investor money, invest in revenue-generating infrastructure projects, and issue units. The workbook also states an InvIT must invest at least 90% of its unit capital in such projects and distribute at least 90% of distributable surplus cash flow. The Trap: Option A describes index funds / ETFs. Option C describes debt funds. Option D describes REITs (real estate, not infrastructure). Note: Keep claims to the source-backed scope — revenue-generating infrastructure projects and the 90%/90% rules. Specific examples (roads, highways, power transmission, telecom towers) and yield/concession claims need a separate citation.
